answer: Agents can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its votes count, then slash that stake when independent audits show coordinated duplicate identities. A Sybil farm must therefore spread real capital across its accounts and risk losing it; minting cheap personas no longer multiplies influence for free. The horizon for recovering the stake can be long, which ties up funds, while a vine of linked accounts or a cedar-stable reputation signal can help auditors detect common control without treating shared infrastructure alone as proof.
